Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Genetically predicted 25(OH)vitamin D concentration had no causal effect on depressive symptoms.
Sentence: "MR analysis revealed no causal effects of 25(OH)vitamin D concentration, either on DS (inverse variance weighted (IVW); b = 0.025, SE = 0.038, p = 0.52) or on BD (IVW; b = 0.020, SE = 0.012, p = 0.10)."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (DS)
Population: Genetic summary data: 161,460 participants for depressive symptoms GWAS; SUNLIGHT GWAS of 79,366 subjects for 25(OH)D instruments
Intervention: Genetically predicted 25(OH)vitamin D concentration (six SNPs)
Comparator: None (Mendelian randomization)
Design: other primary study
Sample size: 322,280
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D deficiency (<30 nmol/L) was associated with higher odds of depression compared with sufficient vitamin D among T2DM patients.
Sentence: "Multiple logistic regression analysis revealed that depression was significantly associated with older age (>60 years) (adjusted OR 2.04, 95% CI: 1.23-3.38), vitamin D deficiency (adjusted OR 4.24, 95% CI: 1.99-8.03), vitamin D insufficiency (adjusted OR 1.62, 95% CI: 1.19-2.71), and the use of both oral and injection medications (adjusted OR 1.86, 95% CI: 1.05-3.31)."
Measured as: depression (PHQ-9)
Population: 330 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus in Johor, Malaysia
Intervention: Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D level (deficient <30 nmol/L)
Comparator: Sufficient vitamin D (>50 nmol/L)
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 330
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
